target_customer: French and European online shoppers who want installment payments at any store without merchant integration
problem: Only about 15 percent of European e-commerce offered buy now pay later, so most shoppers could not split payments.
business_model: Consumer fintech earning a commission from the buyer or merchants, with a virtual card for payment and a refund and repay feature
product_category: Consumer buy now pay later app

founders.name: Yohan Elbase
founders.background_notes: Former M&A director at Haussmann Venture per FrenchWeb.

exit.reason: Joe sold its business assets (fonds de commerce) to La Banque Postale per CFNews

competitors.name: Alma
competitors.what: French pay in installments service for merchants
competitors.traction_then: Main French player; raised 49M EUR in 2021

competitors.name: Klarna
competitors.what: Swedish BNPL leader entering France with a three installment product

competitors.name: Scalapay
competitors.what: Italian BNPL launched in France in late 2020
competitors.traction_then: Acceptance rates reported above 90 percent in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Bank data aggregation for credit scoring, virtual card issuance and collections are standard fintech engineering with regulated, hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded BNPL players and bank backed entrants; the no merchant integration angle was the differentiator and was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: La Banque Postale took over the business in late 2022 and its BNPL subsidiary is branded Django.

market_need_then: French and European BNPL was growing quickly in 2021, with Klarna entering France and Alma and Pledg raising money; Joe itself claimed only about 15 percent of European e-commerce had BNPL.

identity.voice_and_tone: Consumer friendly, positions the app as flexible and tech powered

brand_strength.rationale: Reported 10,000 users shortly after launch, but no press about the brand itself; the app store listing under the same bundle id now shows Django, suggesting the brand did not survive.

outcome_analysis: Joe launched in early 2021 after a 1 million euro angel seed, reporting over 10,000 users, and joined YC for Winter 2022 in a crowded French BNPL market. The business was sold to La Banque Postale in late 2022, about two and a half years after founding, with terms undisclosed. Whether it was a success or a distressed sale is not public.
notes: Seed was 1M EUR (FrenchWeb, 2021-04-07); amount_usd left null rather than converted. Acquisition date 2022-11 comes from CB Insights; CFNews page date was unclear in the snippet. The deal was an asset sale per CFNews. The YC site field was empty and the company website is dead or unknown. The app store listing for the same bundle id now shows Django, which is circumstantial and not recorded as a rebrand. Some sources say Lille rather than Paris.
